description: Variation of conditions 2 (Approved Plans) and 4 (Hard and Soft Landscaping) attached to planning permission ref 2023/1029 dated 26/07/2023 for the renovation of the existing park. The variation would allow amendments to the approved layout, materials, and planting scheme to include a revised path network, consolidated play equipment, updated surfacing materials, and an enhanced biodiversity planting strategy.
decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.
<p>No changes to soil levels within the vicinity of the retained trees shall be undertaken.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To safeguard the retained trees.</p>

<p>No mechanical excavation shall be undertaken within the root protection areas of retained trees, and any required excavation (for example for the provision of fixings for hard landscaping features such as seating or play equipment) shall be undertaken by hand or using an air space.Any roots exposed shall not be severed.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To safeguard the root systems of retained trees.</p>

<p>No hard landscaping features such as benches or play equipment shall be installed within the root protection areas of retained trees until full details of the methods for securing such features have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority.The landscaping features affected shall be installed in full accordance with the details thus approved.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To safeguard the root systems of retained trees.</p>

<div style="">Prior to commencement of development A Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the Local Planning Authority.<br><br>The HMMP must include as a minimum:<br><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">a non-technical summary;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the [HMMP];</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">all landscaping in accordance with the scheme;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">the management measures to maintain habitat shall be carried out for a period of 10 years from the completion of development; and&nbsp;</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">such maintenance to include the replacement of any plants that die, or are severely damaged, seriously diseased, or removed.<br></li></ul>The development shall not be undertaken otherwise than in full accordance with the details approved which shall be carried out within a period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the development,&nbsp;and maintained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.</div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">Notice shall be given, in writing to the Local Planning Authority when the:<br><ul style=""><li style="margin-left: 15px;">HMMP has been implemented within; and</li><li style="margin-left: 15px;">habitat creation and enhancement works as set out in the [HMMP] have been completed.</li></ul>REASON: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain through both on site and off site delivery, in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Hackney’s Local Plan Policy LP47 and London Plan Policy G6.&nbsp;</div>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development, a qualified tree specialist must be appointed to provide arboricultural supervision and inspection. The details of this appointment and the specialist's responsibilities must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submission should include the methodology and programme for reporting, as well as a timetable for inspections.<br style="">The approved works must be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details. Upon completion of the development, a report from the appointed arboriculturist must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, confirming that all tree protection measures and tree works were carried out in accordance with the approved plans accompanied by photographs taken at critical stages.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: to ensure that works affecting trees are carried out in a professional and controlled manner, safeguarding their health and long-term viability. This is in accordance with good arboricultural practice and is supported by BS 5837:2012 and Policy LP51 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033.</p>

<div>Prior to commencement of the development, details of surface water management for the varied works shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. Details shall include: (i) a specification and typical construction build-ups for all new and altered surfacing where permeability is relied upon, (ii) a plan showing the destination and routing of runoff from new and altered hard surfaces, and (iii) a management and maintenance plan for permeable surfaces for the lifetime of the development. The development shall be carried out and thereafter maintained in accordance with the approved details.</div><div><br></div><div>REASON: In the interest of sustainable urban drainage.</div>

<p>A hard and soft landscaping scheme illustrated on detailed drawings shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, in writing, before the development is occupied, for the planting of trees and shrubs showing species, type of stock, numbers of trees and shrubs to be included and showing areas to be grass seeded or turfed, together with details of all boundary treatment, fences and other hard landscaping features; all landscaping in accordance with the scheme, when approved, shall be carried out within a period of twelve months from the date on which the development of the site commences or shall be carried out in the first planting (and seeding) season following completion of the development, and shall be maintained to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority for a period of ten years, such maintenance to include the replacement of any plants that die, or are severely damaged, seriously diseased, or removed.&nbsp;</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To accord with the requirements of Section 197(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and to provide reasonable environmental standards in the interests of the appearance of the site and area.</p>

<div style="">Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, details and full specifications of 3 bird boxes and 3 bat boxes, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:<br></div><div style=""><br>A minimum of 3 bird boxes incorporated into the design of the development, with a variety of box types (including different sized entrance holes) to provide habitat for diverse bird species. The boxes should be between 3 and 5 metres from the ground. The boxes should be facing north, east or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided). Boxes located in the same area should not be placed too close together.</div><div style="">&nbsp;<br>A minimum of 3 bat boxes incorporated into the design of the development. Boxes should be placed at least 4m above the ground. The boxes should be placed away from artificial light sources and ideally located near dark tree lines or hedgerows where possible. The boxes should be located facing south, southeast or southwest, and exposed to sun for part of the day.</div><div style="">&nbsp;<br>The details hereby approved shall be delivered, in full, prior to the first occupation of the development and shall be maintained for the lifespan of the development.</div><div style=""><br></div><div style="">REASON: To support bird and bat populations in Hackney and preserve endangered urban biodiversity, by providing nesting opportunities, in accordance with Hackney’s Local Plan LP33 policy LP47 which states that all development schemes involving buildings with an eaves height or roof commencement height of 5 metres and above are required to provide nesting boxes for swifts, sparrows, starlings, and/or bats as appropriate.</div>
